clue.text: Parisian artist last seen in "South Pacific'., say

definitions.text: Parisian artist last seen in "South Pacific'., say

parts.words: Parisian artist last seen in "South Pacific'., say
parts.note: a painter born in Paris who spent his last years and died on islands in the South Pacific, punning on the musical's title

explanation.surface: Someone recalls where a French painter was last spotted, as if he had appeared in a Broadway musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title suggests the musical, but the clue means the actual region: the painter ended his days in French Polynesia.
explanation.definitionFit: The post-Impressionist painter was born in Paris and died in the Marquesas Islands of Polynesia.

clue.text: Born with loquacity, the French talk too fast

parts.note: gab is chatter or talkativeness, as in 'gift of the gab'
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone born chatty, like the French, speaks too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak rapidly and unintelligibly is to jabber.

clue.text: Out of bed and ready for toast?

explanation.surface: Someone who has got up is ready for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is that one stands up to propose a toast; the surface suggests bread for breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Having got up from sleep means up, and at a dinner one stands to drink a toast.

clue.text: Linen subject to deterioration

parts.note: under means subject to, as in 'under orders'
wear is damage through use, as in 'wear and tear'

explanation.surface: Bed sheets fray over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linen' means body linen, i.e. clothes worn next to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn beneath clothes were traditionally called body linen.

clue.text: Translating in lesson can be incomprehensible

indicators.note: translating turns words into other forms, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A translation exercise in class may be impossible to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translating' rearranges IN LESSON CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd and making no sense cannot be understood.

clue.text: Witnessed fist fight with woodcutter

parts.note: witnessed means saw, past tense of see
a mill is an old slang word for a boxing match or punch-up

explanation.surface: Someone saw a brawl break out alongside a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: MILL as a fist fight is old boxing slang, still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber yard where logs are sliced into planks by machine is, loosely, a cutter of wood.

clue.text: Interview for Oxford, for example

explanation.surface: An Oxford University interview is one example.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is a diocese, the seat of a bishop, not the university.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone formally is to see them, and a bishop's diocese like Oxford is a see.

clue.text: Ill-bred youth needs women's guidance

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
help is assistance or guidance

explanation.surface: A badly behaved young man needs a woman's guiding hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an impudent young person, a sense of the word for a puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a young dog is also used scornfully of a rude or ill-mannered youngster.

clue.text: Piece of news is first in editor's list

parts.note: an item is a single news report

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the word editor's

explanation.surface: A story is top of the editor's running order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first in' takes E from editor's.
explanation.definitionFit: To set things out one by one is to enumerate them as a list.

clue.text: A title with an original borrowed from the classics

indicators.note: original in the sense of new and inventive, so these letters are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A book title containing an ancient quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges A TITLE and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of Latin derivation come from the language of the ancient Roman authors.

clue.text: Steps taken to counter the new ball

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: In a cricket match, footwork is used to deal with a fresh ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps taken to counter the new ball' reads like batting technique; 'steps' is the definition, a country dance with its set moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural social gathering with folk dancing is a set of steps performed to music.

clue.text: In the outcome, man's first partner has no trumps

parts.note: in Genesis Eve is the partner of Adam, the first man
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: A bridge player's partner ends up bidding a hand with no trump suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's first partner' looks like a card-table phrase, but means the first man's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrases like 'in the event' mean as things turn out, so the word is a synonym for result.

clue.text: Arles distorted in the strong light

indicators.note: distorted tells us the letters of the town's name are bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Provençal town of Arles looks warped in the harsh sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges ARLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A device emitting an intense, narrow beam is a source of powerful illumination.

clue.text: Omission that may be taken as an offence

definitions.text: that may be taken as an offence

explanation.surface: Leaving something out could cause someone to feel insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition relies on the idiom 'take exception', meaning to be offended.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusion from a rule is an omission, and to take it is to feel affronted.

clue.text: Husband is in the bank, she is in hotel work

definitions.text: Husband is in the bank, she is in hotel work

indicators.note: is in tells us one word goes inside the other

parts.note: camber is the banking, or slope, of a road
a woman employed in household or hotel service is a maid

explanation.surface: A married couple split careers: he works at a bank, she in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' places H inside CAMBER; 'bank' suggests money but means the slope of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who cleans and tidies guest rooms works in hotel service.

clue.text: Declaration on foreign articles expressing less than the truth

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the declaration comes after the articles

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite article
un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite article
a declaration is a formal statement

explanation.surface: A declaration about overseas news reports turns out to be economical with the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the declaration after the articles. 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but means grammatical words for 'a' and 'the' in French and German.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something as smaller or milder than it really is amounts to saying less than is so.

clue.text: Prepare to publish report of college leader

parts.note: to edit is to prepare a text for publication

indicators.note: report of says the next word is heard spoken, giving a word of the same pronunciation

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to print an account about the head of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like the college head, but a leader is a newspaper's opinion column.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers the opinion piece stating the paper's view is called a leading article.

clue.text: Caught Asiatic form of neuralgia

indicators.note: form of signals a new shape for these letters, a rearrangement

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone has picked up an Asian strain of nerve pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges C and ASIATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain along the nerve running down the back of the leg is a kind of nerve pain.

clue.text: Make a call here to tighten with a spanner

parts.note: to contract is to draw tighter or shrink
a bridge spans a gap, so it is a spanner

explanation.surface: A mechanic is told to phone in for help tightening a nut with a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' suggests a wrench, but here it is anything that spans. 'call' is a bid in the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Players in this card game bid, or call, during the auction before play.

clue.text: Fruit-cake in a hard container

explanation.surface: A fruit cake kept in a sturdy tin.
explanation.walkthrough: A fruitcake is slang for a crazy person; the second definition describes a nut sitting in its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a crazy person matches fruitcake, and a kernel in its shell is a nut in a case.

clue.text: Stick to the punt — or put your foot in it!

parts.note: to gum is to stick with glue
a punt is a kick, so to boot

explanation.surface: Advice to someone on a punting trip: stay on the boat or risk a soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a flat-bottomed boat, but it means a kick; the definition is literal, a boot one puts a foot in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber wellington is footwear one steps into, the idiom taken literally.

clue.text: Tried to attain pure sound

indicators.note: sound here means the word is heard rather than written, so it matches a word said the same

parts.note: chaste means pure or virtuous

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to produce a clear tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pure sound' suggests a clear note; 'sound' marks the homophone of CHASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue a goal is to go after it, trying to reach it.

clue.text: Meticulous head of Physio is away dealing with joints

indicators.note: is away says that letter has gone missing from the longer word

parts.note: meticulous means particular, fussy about detail

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word Physio

explanation.surface: A fussy chief physiotherapist is absent from a clinic that treats joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is away' removes P (the 'head of' Physio) from PARTICULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the medical term for things relating to the body's joints.

clue.text: Strike to get influence in politics

explanation.surface: Workers walk out to gain political leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow, and political clout means power and pull.

clue.text: Sound of deep brass exuding a vitality

indicators.note: exuding means giving off, so the letter is expelled from the brass noise

parts.note: oompah imitates the low, rhythmic notes of a tuba or brass band

explanation.surface: A tuba player's low notes are full of life and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exuding' removes the A from OOMPAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word for energy and attractive liveliness is a synonym of zest.

clue.text: Idealised mental picture of French friend going back to die

indicators.note: going back tells us the French word is written backwards

parts.note: ami is French for friend
to go is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a perfect image of a French companion returning home to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns AMI into IMA.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis the term means an idealised mental image of a person, often a parent.

clue.text: They press, even with metal clubs

parts.note: even means level or flat
irons are golf clubs with metal heads

explanation.surface: Golfers persist, even using their iron clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like a verb about pushing on, but the definition means devices that press clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned heated smoothing tools are used to press creases out of laundry.

clue.text: Douglas is said to be infirm

indicators.note: is said to be in signals the letters sit within the word infirm, read as 'in firm'

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas is reportedly frail.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the tree, the Douglas fir, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas is a tall North American conifer.

clue.text: One encouraging a punter

parts.note: a punter is someone who places bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: Someone cheers on a gambler at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNTER is British for a gambler; the answer is a variant spelling of 'abettor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abets helps or eggs another person on, so is an encourager.

clue.text: Permit is in fact cancelled

indicators.note: is in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a deed is a fact or action, as in 'in deed'
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A licence is in fact revoked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' sets the permit word inside the word for fact; 'Permit' looks like a noun, a licence, but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossed out or struck from a record means removed, so it is a synonym of erased.
